title: Houses Were Allotted by Lot • The Muhajirun’s Hearts Wept • The Qur’anic Praise of the Ansar • The Night Guest • The Muhajirun’s Gratitude • A Sign of Faith • A Written Document • One Nation, Different Tribes • One Blood, One Judgement • The Neighbour Is Like Oneself

blocks.1: The Muhajirun were arriving one by one. Who would stay in whose house? Even in this question the Ansar did not apply their own preference. Which Ansari would take in which Muhajir, they settled by drawing lots.
blocks.3: The name of ‘Uthman ibn Maz‘un (RA) came up in the lottery to stay in our house, when the Ansar drew lots for the residence of the Muhajirun.{{1}}
blocks.4: No room was left for liking and disliking. Whoever fell to one’s lot became one’s guest. ‘Uthman ibn Maz‘un (RA) stayed in the house of Umm al-‘Ala’ (RA). When he fell ill, that Ansari woman nursed him, to the end.
blocks.6: A home was found, brothers were found. Still the houses of Makkah came to mind. After coming to Madinah, Abu Bakr (RA) and Bilal (RA) fell ill with fever. ‘A’ishah (RA) went to see them.
blocks.8: ‘A’ishah (RA) said: after the Prophet {{1}} came to Madinah, Abu Bakr (RA) and Bilal (RA) were seized by fever. I went to them and said, Father, how are you? Bilal, how are you? When the fever came on, Abu Bakr would say, every man is greeted in the morning among his family, while death is nearer to him than the strap of his sandal. And when the fever left Bilal he would raise his voice and say, Ah, if only I knew, shall I again spend a night in a valley around which will be idhkhir and jalil grass? Shall I again go down to the waters of Majinnah some day? Shall Shamah and Tafil mountains appear before me again? ‘A’ishah said, I went to the Prophet {{2}} and informed him. He said, O Allah, make Madinah as dear to us as we love Makkah, or even more. Make it healthy, bless us in its sa‘ and mudd, and move its fever to Juhfah.{{3}}
blocks.9: One was Bilal (RA), whose voice had said ‘Ahad’ under the whip in Makkah. That very man is now weeping for the grass of Makkah. The Prophet {{1}} did not scold them, nor belittle the memory. The love with which one loves Makkah, he asked the same for Madinah; even more.
blocks.10: The Qur’anic Praise of the Ansar
blocks.11: The Ansar were not alone like Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA). This sharing was the habit of the whole Ansar community. Allah Himself sent down a verse about them.
blocks.13: And those who were already settled in this home (Madinah) and in faith before them, love whoever migrates to them, and feel no need in their hearts for what is given to them (that is, to the Muhajirun), and give them preference over themselves, even though they themselves are in want. In truth, those who are saved from the stinginess of their own selves, they are the successful.{{1}}
blocks.14: Putting others first even in one’s own want; the Qur’an has named this quality ‘ithar’. And it has called this one quality freedom from stinginess, and the key to success. So Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘’s (RA) offer of half his wealth was not a single event; it was the nature mixed into the blood of the whole Ansar community.
blocks.16: This verse is no imagined praise. It came in answer to a true event of one night. A man came to the Prophet {{1}} and said he was hungry. The Prophet {{2}} sent word to his wives’ houses. From every house the same answer came, there is nothing in the house but water.
blocks.18: Then the Messenger of Allah {{1}} said, who will host this one tonight? One of the Ansar said, I. He took the man to his wife and said, honour the guest of the Messenger of Allah {{2}}. The wife said, there is only the children’s food in the house. He said, set out the food, light the lamp, and if the children ask for supper, put them to sleep. The wife did so; she set out the food, lit the lamp, put the children to sleep. Then she got up, pretending to fix the lamp, and put it out. The two made the guest see as if they too were eating; yet that night they themselves passed without eating. In the morning that Ansari went to the Prophet {{3}}. The Prophet {{4}} said, tonight Allah laughed at the deed of you two, or said, was amazed. Then Allah sent down this verse, they give others preference over themselves even though they are in want.{{5}}
blocks.19: The lamp was put out so that the guest would not notice there was so little on the plate. Two people passed a night without eating. And in return came a verse of the Qur’an, which will be recited until the Day of Resurrection. Who that Ansari was, the narration has no name. The name was not kept written; the deed stayed written.
blocks.21: After all this a fear arose in the hearts of the Muhajirun. They came with this fear to the Prophet {{1}} himself.
blocks.23: When the Prophet {{1}} came to Madinah, the Muhajirun came to him and said, O Messenger of Allah, we have not seen a people who can give so much from plenty, nor be so sympathetic from little. Those among whom we have settled have borne the burden of our labour and made us share in their joy. We fear they will take away all the reward. The Prophet {{2}} said, no, as long as you pray to Allah for them and praise them.{{3}}
blocks.24: On one side the love of the Ansar. On the other the gratitude of the Muhajirun; not taking and staying silent, but returning it in du‘a and praise. The Prophet {{1}} gave both sides one task each. Those who received will pray. Those who gave, their reward is not reduced.
blocks.26: About the Ansar the Prophet {{1}} said one thing so briefly that it works like a measuring stick.
blocks.28: The sign of faith is love for the Ansar, and the sign of hypocrisy is hatred for the Ansar.{{1}}
blocks.29: Those who shared their house, land and food; love for them remained a sign of faith.
blocks.31: Brotherhood joined the houses. But when Muslims, Jews, and in their hearts doubtful people live together in one city, love alone does not suffice. The Prophet {{1}} had a document written. A charter; between the Muhajirun, the Ansar, and the Jewish tribes of Madinah.
blocks.32: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} wrote a document between the Muhajirun and the Ansar, in which he included the Jews too, kept them in their religion and wealth, and laid conditions on them, and laid conditions for them.{{2}}
blocks.33: The bond of brotherhood is a matter of the heart. But a city does not run on trust in the heart; there will be misunderstandings, quarrels, an outside enemy will come. So the Prophet {{1}} did not stop at oral understanding. This is no hadith; not an account from the mouth of any Companion. It is the verbatim text of a written document, which Ibn Ishaq has preserved in his Sirah book. Historians know it by the name ‘the Charter of Madinah’; it is counted as one of the first written constitutions of the world.{{2}}
blocks.34: Forty-seven clauses. In each clause a boundary drawn. Who will live with whom, who will give whom security, in a quarrel to whom to go.
blocks.36: The first word of the charter is the biggest declaration.
blocks.38: This written document is from Muhammad the unlettered Prophet, between the believers and Muslims of Quraysh and Yathrib, and those who follow them, join them and strive with them. Truly they are one nation, distinct from other people.{{1}}
blocks.39: The Muhajirun of Quraysh, the Ansar of Yathrib; different in tribe, different in lineage. But in this one line they became one nation. Then each tribe was written separately; Banu ‘Awf, Banu al-Harith, Banu Sa‘idah, Banu Jusham, Banu al-Najjar, Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf, Banu al-Nabit, Banu Aws. Each by its own old rules would bear one another’s blood-money, and share the cost of freeing captives fairly.{{1}}
blocks.40: The old tribal structure was not broken. Only a new roof was placed over it; the roof of justice. One clause states plainly,
blocks.42: And the believers shall not abandon among themselves one burdened by debt or crushed by the weight of many dependants; in the matter of ransom or blood-money, they shall give to him according to custom.{{1}}
blocks.43: If someone fell into debt, if someone fell into calamity, his tribe could not abandon him. This was the state’s first social security.
blocks.45: In the middle clauses of the charter, the matters of justice and security.
blocks.47: And no believer shall kill a believer for the sake of a disbeliever, nor help a disbeliever against a believer. And the protection of Allah is one; the lowest of them can give refuge. And the believers are friends of one another, to the exclusion of other people. And whoever of the Jews follows us shall have help and equal treatment; they shall not be wronged, nor shall anyone be helped against them. And the peace of the believers is one; in war in the way of Allah no believer shall make peace without the other believers, except on terms of equality and justice. And every party that goes out on an expedition with us shall relieve one another in turn. And in the blood shed in the way of Allah, the believers are equal sharers with one another; and the God-fearing believers are on the best and straightest path.{{1}}
blocks.48: The price of a believer’s life will not be measured by the tribe; no killing of a believer for a disbeliever’s interest, and in blood shed in the way of Allah all are equal sharers. And if a quarrel grew into a riot?
blocks.50: And in whatever matter you differ, its decision returns to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to Muhammad.{{1}}
blocks.51: Not the personal wish of a tribal chief, not the strength of the sword; judgement would go to a fixed address. The way to stop the cycle of blood-revenge of Arabia is in this one line. Another clause tells for whom the city is safe, for whom not.
blocks.53: And it is not lawful for a believer who has affirmed what is in this document and believes in Allah and the Last Day, to help or shelter one who commits a new crime. And whoever helps or shelters him, upon him is the curse and wrath of Allah on the Day of Resurrection; from him no obligatory or voluntary act will be accepted.{{1}}
blocks.54: Shelter only for the innocent. To cover up a criminal is to stand against the whole charter.
blocks.56: One small clause of the charter almost escapes the eye, yet its weight is great.
blocks.58: And the neighbour is like oneself; not to be harmed, and not a sinner.{{1}}
blocks.59: The neighbour is like oneself; in this one comparison the whole responsibility is understood. I do not harm myself. Not harming the neighbour is to be just the same. The same thing the Prophet {{1}} said later in another way,
blocks.60: By Allah, he does not believe! By Allah, he does not believe! By Allah, he does not believe! It was asked, who, O Messenger of Allah? He said, the one whose neighbour is not safe from their harm.{{1}}
blocks.61: A word said with a threefold oath. The neighbour’s safety is the measure of faith.

footnotes.2: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, Surah al-Hashr 59:9, pp. 516–517 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.3: Sahih al-Bukhari 3798 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA)); to the same effect Sahih Muslim 2054
footnotes.4: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 2487 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA); Imam al-Tirmidhi: hadithun sahihun hasanun gharib); to the same effect Sunan Abi Dawud 4812
footnotes.6: Ibn Ishaq, al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (in the narration of Ibn Hisham); Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Dustur al-Madinah’
footnotes.7: The nature and chain of the Charter of Madinah: it is not a saying narrated with a chain like a hadith, but the text of a written document preserved by Ibn Ishaq (d. 151 AH) in his Sirah book. Ibn Hisham compiled it from Ibn Ishaq. No manuscript of the original document survives; the text preserved by Ibn Ishaq is the only source. Most modern researchers regard its core content as historically reliable, since it bears no influence of the ideas current in later times. In this dars it is presented not as a hadith with a chain but as a document of the Sirah.

quiz.q: Which quality of the Ansar is praised in Surah al-Hashr 59:9?
o: Putting others before oneself even in one’s own want (ithar)
Showing bravery in war, which recalls the events of Badr and Uhud
Praying much at night, which recalls the prayer of the night of the Mi‘raj
Earning much wealth

quiz.q: The phrase of the verse ‘those saved from stinginess are the successful’ matches which conduct of the Ansar?
o: ‘Abd al-Rahman’s (RA) going to the market, which speaks of seeking the road to the market
Salman’s (RA) fasting, which speaks of voluntary fasting worship
Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘’s (RA) offer of half the wealth
Bilal’s (RA) giving the adhan, which speaks of the first sound of the adhan
quiz.e: The verse was revealed in praise of the Ansar’s quality of ithar.

quiz.q: Someone helps a person in distress and then taunts them. In the light of Surah al-Hashr 59:9, how is this?
o: Not true ithar; a sign of not being freed from stinginess
This is natural, because the helper has a right
This matches the Ansar’s way, although the Ansar truly showed this quality
The reward increases by it, although the promise of reward is in the verse in a different way
quiz.e: In the verse freedom from stinginess itself is called success.

quiz.q: What exactly is the Charter of Madinah?
o: A hadith, narrated directly with a chain from a Companion
The text of a written document preserved in Ibn Ishaq’s Sirah book
A verse of the Qur’an, although it has no continuity of chain
A summary of the Prophet’s ﷺ oral speech, although it was written in Arabic itself
quiz.e: Not a hadith from the mouth of any Companion, but the verbatim text of a document.

quiz.q: Why is the Charter of Madinah called a ‘document’ rather than a ‘hadith’?
o: Because it is part of the Qur’an, although the sentences of the charter begin in the name of the Prophet ﷺ
Because no Companion wrote it, although many rulings of the Qur’an were being revealed at the same time
Because it is not written in Arabic
Because it is not a saying narrated with a chain, but a written text preserved by Ibn Ishaq
quiz.e: This distinction between hadith and document is important for verification.

quiz.q: An organisation has no written rules, only oral understanding. What can be learned from the Charter of Madinah?
o: Oral understanding is enough, although oral understanding is also a kind of promise
Written rules are a sign of distrust, although the Charter of Madinah itself was made in writing
Having no rules is freedom
To make a written document instead of stopping at oral understanding
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ did not stop at a word of promise; he had it written.

quiz.q: What is declared in the first clause of the Charter of Madinah?
o: Only Muslims can live in Madinah, although the charter included the Jews too
Each tribe will be counted as a separate state
The Muhajirun and Ansar are one nation distinct from all other people
No dispute can be settled without war, although the old rules of each tribe were kept

quiz.q: According to the charter, what happens if a believer falls into debt?
o: They will be expelled from the tribe
Their wealth will be confiscated, which is written nowhere in the charter
They must repay the debt alone, which speaks only of the ransom of war captives
The believers will not deprive them of giving, according to custom

quiz.q: How was the old tribal structure used in the charter?
o: The tribal structure was not broken
All tribes were broken to make one tribe
The power of tribal chiefs was increased
Competition between tribes was encouraged
quiz.e: In clauses 2–10 the old rules of each tribe were kept.

quiz.q: According to the charter, where should one go to settle a dispute?
o: To Allah and Muhammad ﷺ
To the tribal chief, which is in no clause of the charter
To the richest person, which would have created dependence on a neighbouring tribe
To the arbitration of a neighbouring tribe

quiz.q: What does the charter say about killing a believer?
o: The punishment for killing a rich believer will be greater, which is not in the charter
No believer will kill another believer for the sake of a disbeliever
Only the killing of the Ansar will be judged, which is not in the charter
Rules of killing will differ by tribe, which is not in the charter

quiz.q: Why is the condition of ‘returning to Allah and Muhammad ﷺ’ for settling a dispute important?
o: It shows that judgement always went in the Prophet’s ﷺ favour, although that was exactly what was customary in the pre-Islamic era
It speaks of judgement going to a fixed address instead of the tribal chief’s wish or the sword
It increases the power of tribal chiefs, which would have reduced the power of tribal chiefs
It increases war further, although in reality that often happened
quiz.e: A step toward stopping the cycle of blood-revenge of Arabia.

quiz.q: In an area, people go to fighting to settle a dispute. Which clause of the Charter of Madinah can be applied?
o: Returning the dispute to Allah and His Messenger (today, the principles of the din), which is a path opposite to the principle of the charter
Accepting the word of the stronger party, which is a method opposite to clause 23 of the charter
Avoiding the dispute, which is a method opposite to clause 23 of the charter
Each judging for themselves

quiz.q: What does the Charter of Madinah say about the neighbour?
o: The neighbour has a right in one’s wealth
The neighbour must always be given food
The neighbour is like oneself
There is no instruction about the neighbour

quiz.q: Saying ‘By Allah, he does not believe’ three times, whom did the Prophet ﷺ speak of?
o: One who does not pray, although there is a different hadith about prayer
One who does not fast, although there is a different hadith about fasting
One who does not give zakat, although there is a different hadith about zakat
The one whose neighbour is not safe from their harm

quiz.q: What do the clause ‘the neighbour is like oneself’ and the hadith ‘one whose neighbour is not safe does not believe’ show together?
o: The two are opposed to each other, although both are in fact true claims
The hadith was added after the charter
The written law and the Prophet’s ﷺ word give the same message in two ways
Only the Muslim neighbour is spoken of, although the hadith speaks of all neighbours
quiz.e: The same value has come in the law and in the hadith in two ways.

quiz.q: A person is indifferent to their neighbour’s distress. Combining the Charter of Madinah and the hadith, what can be said to them?
o: The neighbour’s distress is the neighbour’s own responsibility
It is better to keep no relation with the neighbour
There is no guidance in Islam about the neighbour
The neighbour is like oneself
quiz.e: Dustur al-Madinah clause 40 and Sahih al-Bukhari 6016.
